injuries.description: cracked fracture of the skull on the right parietal region
source: cracked fracture of the skull on the right parietal region.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of parietal bone of skull

injuries.description: contusion of the brain and brain stem injury
source: The clinical diagnosis was contusion of the brain and brain stem injury.

injuries.description: permanent brain damage to the parietal area resulting in parietal lobe dysfunction
source: damage to the parietal region sustained in the accident has resulted in the parietal lobe function being abnormal and inefficient.
Permanent disability in the form of impaired intelligence, poor co-ordination of his four limbs and defects in his speech will be expected.

manifestations.description: totally unconscious for a period of ten days
remained "drowsy" a further period of two weeks after regaining consciousness
unable to sit up as the supporting muscles had weakened
slurred speech / speech affected / defects in his speech
unsteady gait / clumsiness in walking / natural clumsiness of movement
impaired intelligence / intellectual impairment / I.Q. below average
poor co-ordination of his four limbs
disturbance of the sense of balance
disinclination to speak / unwilling to talk / inhibited in his use of speech
loss of ability to write fluently / writing skill had deteriorated
loss of powers of concentration / poor concentration / inattention and frustration
abnormal electro-encephalograms indicating a strong possibility that epileptic attacks or epileptic disturbances might develop
red eyes and toothache (reported by father)

treatments_received: admitted to the Neuro-surgical Unit of Queen Elizabeth Hospital
follow-up clinic attendance up to 14th June, 1975
examinations by neurologists, psychologists and psychiatrists

losses.category: Loss of ability to pursue education
losses.description: Interruption and delay of emotional and intellectual development; loss of ability to learn during formative years; will require special educational provision and will remain behind peers in communication skills and school progress.
Poor co-ordination and natural clumsiness of movement as a result of parietal area damage.
